entries.definition: (used of color) artificially produced; not natural
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the colour in deep rather than on the surface, more concrete than *colored* and no harsher for it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes that arrangement a performance put on for an onlooker, so what looked spontaneous reads as put-up — the accusation *arranged* stops short of.
examples: one of those artfully staged photographs

entries.definition: using artistic forms and conventions to create effects; not natural or spontaneous
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The one here that can name a deliberate artistic manner rather than a failure, where *unlifelike* is only a falling short.
examples: a stylized mode of theater production

entries.definition: artificial as if portrayed in a film
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Manufactured-feeling rather than lived — the same screen-thin unreality as *celluloid*, without the sheen.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A plain report of the shortfall, measuring the thing against life and finding it thin, with none of *cardboard*'s contempt.

entries.definition: contrived by art rather than nature
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Denies the thing any standing in reality at all, where *artificial* only reports how it came to be.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the fault on the surface - a mark on something otherwise sound, where *flawed* lets the fault run through it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grades speech or writing as falling short of fluent - a shortfall in the language itself, not *defective*'s fault built into a thing.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says errors and alterations have got in, so the thing can no longer be trusted as it stands - heavier than *flawed*, which admits a fault without unsettling the whole.
examples: spoke a corrupted version of the language

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The participle points back at a sound original that errors have since entered, where *corrupt* simply reports the state.
examples: spoke a corrupted version of the language

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the defect as a verdict on the whole item - colder and more final than *faulty*.
examples: I returned the appliance because it was defective

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Workaday and remediable - it locates a fault to be put right rather than writing the thing off the way *defective* does.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same defect read as structural rather than a spot, which is why it lands harder than *blemished*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word for falling short of perfect - it states the shortfall and stops there, without *defective*'s implication that something inside has gone wrong.
examples: had only an imperfect understanding of his responsibilities

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a statement of capacity - it says imperfection could be introduced and passes no judgement, where *defective* and *corrupt* both condemn.

entries.definition: failing to meet a standard of manufacture due to an imperfection
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grades an item as missing the standard of manufacture, registering the imperfection while cushioning it - far short of calling it *defective*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and total - it leaves the notion nothing salvageable, where *impractical* leaves it merely unworkable.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - it casts the unsoundness as thinking abandoned before it was finished, faulting the effort as much as the result.

entries.definition: not practical; not workable or not given to practical matters
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain term of the family - it states the unworkability and stops there, without the ridicule *crazy* and *half-baked* carry.
examples: refloating the ship proved impractical because of the expense
he is intelligent but too impractical for commercial work

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The barest of these spellings, and the shortness suits a word that makes no argument, only a verdict.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A variant spelling of *meshugge* and no gentler for it - the same unadorned charge of senselessness.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Colloquial and flat - it calls the thing senseless outright, with none of the picture-making *half-baked* offers.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The extra syllables give it a flourish the shorter spellings lack, but the judgement of senselessness is unchanged.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Another form of the same dismissal - senselessness stated as settled fact, where *quixotic* would at least credit an aim.

entries.definition: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the want of practical sense while crediting the ideals behind it, so the disapproval comes out half-admiring.
examples: as quixotic as a restoration of medieval knighthood

entries.definition: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of these - the unrealism is charged to an idealizing temperament rather than a defect, and can be said almost fondly.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flippant - the foolishness is treated as entertaining eccentricity, so it stings less than *crazy* at the same verdict.
examples: a screwball proposal without a prayer of working

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Insulting in a way the others are not - it puts the unsoundness down to a mind too soft to hold a firm thought.

entries.definition: not related to or suitable for everyday needs or activities
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Carries no verdict at all - it records unsuitability for everyday needs where *impractical* implies a fault.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Locates the trouble in the handling rather than in anyone's judgement, so a thoroughly sensible thing can still earn it.

entries.definition: not sensible about practical matters; idealistic and unrealistic
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts a look of fanaticism on the same unrealism, so where *romantic* indulges it this one warns against it.
examples: a wild-eyed dream of a world state

entries.definition: (of plants) bearing or characterized by aments or catkins
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Places a plant by the catkins that characterize it, as flatly as *amentiferous* and with as little praise in it.

entries.definition: (of plants) bearing or characterized by aments or catkins
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and classifying: it records that the plant carries catkins and offers no verdict at all on how much it yields.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A settled favourable verdict on land, but only that it could be farmed well - potential where *rich* asserts the yield itself.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: States the same promise as *arable* transparently through the act of cultivating, so it reads as an open possibility rather than a standing classification of the land.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Heavier and more literal than *cultivable*, claiming no more than that the work of cultivation can be done here.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Elevated praise for a mind that generates abundantly, richer and more admiring than a flat *productive*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises a mind as ground ideas grow from - readiness and promise, where *prolific* counts what has actually come out of it.

entries.definition: of animals having fur (especially of commercial quality)
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Coolly appraising rather than approving - it marks an animal as carrying fur worth having, without any compliment to the animal.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A bare compound naming what the plant puts out, with none of the claim about quantity that *productive* carries.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Says only that oil is present inside - containing rather than yielding, so nothing is being produced here at all.

entries.definition: producing or capable of producing (especially abundantly)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plain approval of output that covers both actual yield and the bare capacity for it, where *prolific* insists the yield is already there.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Admiration measured by sheer quantity of intellectual output, where *fecund* admires its richness instead.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Short, everyday and emphatic, asserting abundance outright where *productive* still allows mere capacity.

entries.definition: (of farmland) capable of being farmed productively
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most physical of the land words, tying the ground's promise to the labour of tilling it where *arable* keeps the judgement abstract.

entries.definition: not adhering to ethical or moral principles
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Contemptuous - it ranks the character as low, not merely at fault, where *immoral* records the failure and leaves the person's standing alone.
examples: a base, degrading way of life

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States the desert rather than colouring it - the thing has earned rebuke, and the word says so and stops.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight of a legal charge behind a censure that is moral rather than legal, which makes it an outcry where *condemnable* is a ruling.

entries.definition: bringing or deserving severe rebuke or censure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Voices the disapproval as dismay - the thing is bad enough to be lamented, not merely bad enough to be rebuked.

entries.definition: not adhering to ethical or moral principles
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat categorical charge: measured against a standard and found outside it, with the force sitting in the standard rather than in the tone.
